content.title: Add a configured product with a valid non-1 quantity and see the cart update correctly
content.intent: Prove that a shopper can add a valid product after selecting required options, receive a success confirmation, see the header cart signals update, and have the entered non-1 quantity carry into the cart exactly.
content.technique_notes: Derived from happy-path reading of retail-storefront REQ-03 with techniques: eqp for a valid configured product and a valid non-1 quantity representative; state_flow not applicable because the source does not define a gated multi-step wizard; bva considered but not applied because the source gives no quantity bounds and the owner chose valid-quantity coverage only for now; risk-judged strength=3 because money applies, but no combinatorial expansion was needed because the path has one outcome-bearing representative combination.

content.title: Attempt to add a product while a required option is still missing
content.intent: Prove that add to cart is blocked until required options are selected and that the shopper is told which required option is missing.
content.technique_notes: Derived from the REQ-03 missing-option rule using negative/error technique plus eqp for the representative invalid state 'at least one required option missing'; bva not applicable because no option-count limits are specified; risk-judged strength=3 because the add-to-cart gate protects basket correctness, but no combinatorial expansion was needed because one representative invalid state proves the promised outcome.

content.title: Open a product from a listing and inspect its buying information
content.intent: Prove that opening a product from a listing reveals the product information a shopper needs to decide whether to buy.
content.technique_notes: Derived from the REQ-03 product-detail display rule using eqp for a representative listed product; search-list and stateful-flow profiles were not applicable because this path starts from an existing listing result and asserts product-detail rendering rather than list semantics or a wizard; risk-judged strength=2 would suffice for display-only content, but no input combination model was needed because the path has no independent outcome-bearing inputs.

parameters.entry_path: open a product from a listing

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it covers the most financially risky path: correct item, correct quantity, confirmation, and header update on a successful add.
[value_score] Next-highest value because blocking an invalid add and naming the missing option prevents corrupted or misleading cart state.
[value_score] Lower than the add paths because it is display-only, but still required since product detail visibility is explicitly promised and is a prerequisite user decision point.
